title: Draft regulations relating to IIB (Draft Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Insurance Information Bureau of India) Regulations, 2021)
date_verification: Date matches the IRDAI Exposure Drafts listing 'Last Updated' column (08-09-2021) and the filename suffix '2021-09-08'; document itself carries no printed dateline (scanned copy), so confidence is medium rather than high.
extracted_claims: The draft regulation would empower the Insurance Information Bureau of India (IIB) to collect data from regulated entities on the Authority's behalf and specify IIB's objectives, functions and obligations.
The draft would prescribe standards of compliance for regulated entities' submission of data to IIB.
IIB is defined in the draft as the Insurance Information Bureau of India established under the A.P. Societies Registration Act, 2001.
content_excerpt: (Draft) Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Insurance Information Bureau of India) Regulations, 2021. In exercise of the powers conferred by clauses (e) and (f) of sub section (2) of section 14 of IRDAI Act, 1999, the Authority in consultation with the Insurance Advisory Committee, hereby makes the following regulations. 1. Short Title and Commencement... 2. Objective: (a) To clearly specify the Objectives, Functions and Obligations of Insurance Information Bureau and to this end empower IIB to collect Data from the regulated entities on behalf of the Authority. (b) To provide the Standards of Compliance requirements for Regulated Entities towards Submission of Data to IIB. 3. Definitions: (a) 'IIB' means the Insurance Information Bureau of India established under the A.P. Societies Registration Act, 2001.

title: Exposure Draft: Guidelines on Remuneration of Non-Executive Directors and Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer/Whole-time Directors of Insurance companies
date_verification: Date matches IRDAI Exposure Drafts listing 'Last Updated' column (03-01-2022); PDF filename embeds the same date pattern used consistently across this listing.
extracted_claims: The draft proposes to replace the 2016 circular on remuneration of NEDs and MD/CEO/WTDs of insurers, citing five years of experience and a need to avoid compensation structures that reward excessive risk-taking.
For Non-Executive Directors, fixed remuneration (beyond sitting fees) is capped at Rs 20 lakh per annum per director (excluding Chairman), with NEDs ineligible for ESOPs without Authority approval.

For Whole-time Directors/CEOs/MDs, variable pay must be at least 50% of total remuneration (max 300% of fixed pay), with 50% of variable pay deferred over three years (no deferment if variable pay is under Rs 15 lakh) and subject to malus/clawback.
Tenure limits for MD&CEO and WTDs are proposed to be aligned with RBI's stipulations for bank directors.
content_excerpt: Exposure Draft. Guidelines on Remuneration of Non-Executive Directors and Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer/Whole-time Directors of Insurance companies. In order to ensure sound remuneration or compensation practices and avoid situations resulting from excessive risk taking behavior due to inappropriate compensation structures... it is proposed to replace the extant guidelines... issued vide circular ref IRDA/F&A/GDL/LSTD/155/08/2016 dated 05.08.2016. ...For Non-Executive Directors (NEDs): remuneration...shall not exceed Rs. Twenty lakh per annum for each such director excluding Chairman... NEDs shall not be eligible for ESOPs. ...For Whole Time Directors/Chief Executive/Managing Directors: at least 50% of the remuneration subject to maximum 300% of the fixed pay... Minimum of 50% of the variable pay must be deferred... over a period of three years.

title: DRAFT Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Third Party Administrators - Health Services) (Amendment) Regulations, 2022
date_verification: Date matches IRDAI Exposure Drafts listing 'Last Updated' column (16-02-2022).
extracted_claims: The draft amends eligibility criteria for TPA directors, requiring at least one director to be a qualified Medical Practitioner as defined in the Guidelines on Standardization in Health Insurance.
Every TPA would be required to appoint a Chief Executive Officer or Chief Administrative Officer from among its directors/senior employees, and a full-time Chief Medical Officer.

title: Exposure Draft on Group Insurance Products under Health Insurance Business and other operational matters

title: Exposure Draft - Expenses of Management of Insurers transacting life insurance business (draft Regulations, 2022)
date_verification: Date matches IRDAI Exposure Drafts listing 'Last Updated' column (02-08-2022); corroborated by the 23-11-2022 revised draft's own foreword, which states 'the exposure draft of the EoM-Life Regulations 2022 was placed on the website...seeking comments...on 02.08.2022'.
extracted_claims: The draft would insert a single overall Expenses of Management limit for life insurers, replacing existing segmental/sub-segmental limits.

'Expenses of Management' is defined to include operating expenses such as commission, remuneration/brokerage and rewards to agents/intermediaries and reinsurance-inward commission, charged to the Revenue Account.
The Regulations would come into force from the date of publication in the Official Gazette and apply to insurers transacting life insurance business in India.
